SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What is a neighbouring county? (1 mark)
   A. The biggest county
   B. A county that shares a boundary with your county
   C. A county with the same name
   D. A county in another country

2. Which valley runs from north to south through Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. The Tana Valley
   B. The Great Rift Valley
   C. The Coast Valley
   D. The Kisumu Valley

3. What is a plain? (1 mark)
   A. A steep mountain
   B. A waterfall
   C. A lake with salt water
   D. Wide flat land

4. Which lake is the largest lake in Africa and is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Baringo
   B. Lake Victoria
   C. Lake Naivasha
   D. Lake Nakuru

5. What is a lake? (1 mark)
   A. A long channel of flowing water
   B. A very high mountain
   C. A large area of water surrounded by land
   D. A dry plain

6. In many parts of Kenya, when do the long rains usually come? (1 mark)
   A. January to February
   B. September only
   C. June to August
   D. March to May

7. What might happen if all drivers stopped working? (1 mark)
   A. Schools would close forever
   B. Nothing would change
   C. More crops would grow
   D. Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals

8. Which of these is a good? (1 mark)
   A. Teaching
   B. Nursing
   C. Driving a matatu
   D. A pair of shoes

9. Which is a reason why fewer people live in a forest reserve? (1 mark)
   A. There are too many houses
   B. It has many towns
   C. People are not allowed to settle there
   D. It has good roads

10. On a dot map where one dot means 500 people, an area has 4 dots. How many people live there? (1 mark)
   A. 20,000
   B. 2,000
   C. 4,500
   D. 400

11. Which pattern describes people living along a road or river in a line? (1 mark)
   A. Linear
   B. Circular
   C. Clustered
   D. Scattered

12. Which game is played with seeds or stones moved between holes in a board? (1 mark)
   A. Athletics
   B. Bao
   C. Football
   D. Netball

13. Why do we recite the school motto? (1 mark)
   A. To scare others
   B. To waste time
   C. To remember what the school stands for
   D. To hide

14. Which of these is a benefit of economic activities? (1 mark)
   A. They make people poor
   B. They give people jobs and income
   C. They stop trade
   D. They close schools

15. What is one way factories can protect the environment? (1 mark)
   A. Treat waste before releasing it
   B. Burn tyres
   C. Throw waste into rivers
   D. Cut all trees

16. What is a product? (1 mark)
   A. A tool
   B. A worker
   C. A raw material
   D. A finished good that is made

17. Why are sugar factories usually built near cane farms? (1 mark)
   A. Farmers do not like factories
   B. Sugar cannot be sold
   C. Cane is hard to find
   D. Cane is heavy and costly to carry far

18. What is profit? (1 mark)
   A. Money left after paying all costs
   B. The price of a book
   C. Money borrowed
   D. All the money spent

19. Who keeps the money and records it in a school project? (1 mark)
   A. The treasurer
   B. The visitor
   C. The safety officer
   D. The gatekeeper

20. What is a good thing to do at the end of a project? (1 mark)
   A. Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   B. Throw away records
   C. Forget about it
   D. Blame others

21. What is personal protective equipment used for? (1 mark)
   A. To protect a person from harm
   B. To slow down work
   C. To make noise
   D. To hide

22. Which of these is a way of living in peace with others? (1 mark)
   A. Sharing what you have
   B. Cheating
   C. Teasing
   D. Grabbing things

23. When talking about a conflict, which kind of sentence is best? (1 mark)
   A. You are stupid
   B. Everyone hates you
   C. I felt hurt when...
   D. I will hit you

24. What is a responsibility? (1 mark)
   A. A gift
   B. A toy
   C. A duty you should do
   D. A secret

25. Which of these is a correct body safety rule? (1 mark)
   A. Keep it a secret if someone does
   B. Anyone can touch them
   C. No one should touch your private parts
   D. Say nothing

26. What is a suggestion box used for? (1 mark)
   A. Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   B. Keeping food
   C. Storing books
   D. Collecting rubbish

27. Which quality means treating everyone equally? (1 mark)
   A. Fairness
   B. Selfishness
   C. Boasting
   D. Greed

28. Who is a leader? (1 mark)
   A. A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   B. A stranger
   C. A person who breaks rules
   D. A machine

29. Why do we have county governments? (1 mark)
   A. To close schools
   B. To end services
   C. To bring services closer to the people
   D. To stop elections

30. What is public participation? (1 mark)
   A. Citizens hiding
   B. Citizens breaking laws
   C. Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   D. Citizens leaving

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. Give three ways of conserving natural resources. (3 marks)

32. Give four qualities of a good pupil leader. (4 marks)

33. State three ways in which physical features are important to people. (3 marks)

34. Explain why children must not be forced to do hard work. (3 marks)

35. Describe what people do in the cold season to stay healthy and warm. (4 marks)

36. Explain how a historic place such as Fort Jesus helps local people to earn a living. (4 marks)

37. Explain why Kenya does not have summer and winter. (2 marks)

38. Name three natural resources found in Kenya and say how each is used. (3 marks)

39. Give three ways in which the rainy season helps people. (3 marks)

40. A group spent Ksh 350 on seeds and Ksh 150 on tools. They sold vegetables for Ksh 800. Find the profit. Show working. (3 marks)

41. Explain four ways in which rainy weather makes roads dangerous. (4 marks)

42. List four democratic processes in a school. (4 marks)

43. Explain the difference between the size of a county and its population. (3 marks)

44. Explain the difference between a ceremony and a festival and give one example of each. (4 marks)

45. Explain why buying votes with sweets is wrong. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — A county that shares a boundary with your county
   Neighbouring counties touch each other along a boundary.

2. B — The Great Rift Valley
   The Great Rift Valley runs through Kenya.

3. D — Wide flat land
   A plain is a wide, flat area.

4. B — Lake Victoria
   Lake Victoria is shared by three countries.

5. C — A large area of water surrounded by land
   A lake has land all around it.

6. D — March to May
   The long rains are usually from March to May.

7. D — Food and medicine could not reach shops and hospitals
   Transport connects producers, shops and hospitals.

8. D — A pair of shoes
   Goods are things we can touch and use.

9. C — People are not allowed to settle there
   Forest reserves are protected.

10. B — 2,000
   4 x 500 = 2,000.

11. A — Linear
   Linear means in a line.

12. B — Bao
   Bao is a board game with seeds.

13. C — To remember what the school stands for
   Reciting reminds us of the school's aims.

14. B — They give people jobs and income
   Economic activities provide income and food.

15. A — Treat waste before releasing it
   Treating waste avoids pollution.

16. D — A finished good that is made
   Products are the goods that come out of a factory.

17. D — Cane is heavy and costly to carry far
   Being near saves transport costs.

18. A — Money left after paying all costs
   Profit = income - costs.

19. A — The treasurer
   The treasurer handles and records money.

20. A — Evaluate what went well and what to improve
   Evaluation helps us do better next time.

21. A — To protect a person from harm
   PPE protects the wearer.

22. A — Sharing what you have
   Sharing shows kindness.

23. C — I felt hurt when...
   'I' sentences share feelings without blaming.

24. C — A duty you should do
   Rights come with responsibilities.

25. C — No one should touch your private parts
   Your body belongs to you.

26. A — Pupils drop ideas and complaints
   It lets everyone share ideas.

27. A — Fairness
   Fair leaders treat all equally.

28. A — A person who guides and helps others to do something good
   Leaders guide and help.

29. C — To bring services closer to the people
   Counties bring services near to people.

30. C — Citizens giving their views on plans and the budget
   People take part in decisions.

SECTION B
----
31. (3 marks)
   Answer: Plant trees, save water, and reduce waste by reusing and recycling.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each way.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: Honest, fair, responsible and a good listener. Accept humble or hard working.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each quality.

33. (3 marks)
   Answer: They give water, they provide fish and food, and they attract visitors. Accept farming land or electric power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: It harms their health, it stops them going to school, and it is child labour, which is against the law.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each reason.

35. (4 marks)
   Answer: They wear warm clothes, eat and drink hot foods, sleep under blankets, and wash their hands to avoid colds and flu.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct action.

36. (4 marks)
   Answer: Visitors pay entry fees, guides are employed, hotels and restaurants get customers, and craft sellers sell to tourists.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

37. (2 marks)
   Answer: Kenya lies on the equator, so the temperature changes little through the year. Our seasons depend mainly on rain and on how high the land is.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the equator idea, 1 mark for rain or height.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: Water is used for drinking and farming. Land is used for farming and grazing. Minerals such as soda ash are used in factories.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each resource with a use.

39. (3 marks)
   Answer: Crops grow, grass grows for animals, and rivers and tanks fill with water.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Ksh 300.
   Working / marking points: Cost = 350 + 150 = 500. Profit = 800 - 500 = 300. 1 mark for cost, 1 mark for subtraction, 1 mark for answer.

41. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roads become slippery, it is harder to see, floods can sweep away people and vehicles, and water can hide holes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct way.

42. (4 marks)
   Answer: Electing class monitors, class meetings, using a suggestion box, and voting on decisions.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each process.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Size is the area of land a county covers. Population is the number of people who live there. A big county can have few people.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for size, 1 mark for population, 1 mark for the difference or example.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: A ceremony marks a special event in life, such as a wedding. A festival is a big celebration with many people, such as the Lamu Cultural Festival.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each meaning and 1 mark for each example.

45. (3 marks)
   Answer: It is cheating, it makes the election unfair, and votes should be given freely on merit.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.
